full_judgment:
2. The plaintiffs brought the suit stating inter alia that the suit land described in schedule A of the plaint originally belonged to Rajendra Narayan Nondi in 16 annas share with possession, accordingly, CS khatian was prepared in his favour, thereafter one Akhil. Chandra Dhar raised claim over the said land, therefore, litigation cropped up in between the heirs of Rajendra Nondi in one side and said Akhil Chandra Dhar on the other and at one stage the widow of Rajendra Narayan Nondi, namely, Sreemati Promoda Sundori Daishya, having been appointed as guardian of her two minor sons Norendra Nondi and Khagendra Narayan Nondi, admitted that said Akhil Chandra Dhar was the owner of the property described in schedule A to the plaint, therefore, she executed a Nadabi Nama in favour of Akhil Chandra Dhar on 22-7-1924 and got it registered; thereafter Okil Chandra Dhar being the owner in possession of schedule A property sold the same in favour of Jotindra Mohan Chattaijhee and Sheta Nath Banerjhee by a registered kabala dated 28-7-1925; the said Jotindra Nath Chatterjhee and Shetta Nath Banerjhee as purchasers having been in possession of the schedule A property got the same partitioned amicably whereupon Sheta Nath Banarjhee got a sham of 1 Bigha 19 Khatas and 15.48 chattak and the remaining area fell in the sham of Jotindra Mohan; Jotindra Mohan got the B schedule property in his exclusive possession, upon amicable partition with Sheta Nath Banarjhee and while he was in possession entered into an agreement for sale thereof on 16-1-1994 in favour of Bama Charan Paul; Bolo Ram Paul, Horo Lal Paul and Gopal Paul, thereafter, by a registered Kabala dated 25-7-44 transferred the schedule B property in favour of the said Bama Charan Paul, and his three brothers handed over possession; thereafter Bama Charan Paul and the others sold the B schedule property to Hafizuddin the predecessor of plaintiff Nos. 1-10, Taheruddin the predecessor of plaintiff Nos. 11-16 and Hajee Afseruddin the predecessor of plaintiff Nos. 17-26 by a registered kabala dated 16-8-52; after purchase of B schedule property, the predecessors of the plaintiffs applied for permission from the DIT on 11-1-64 for the construction of three-storied pucca building over the suit plot No. 76 and when construction of the said building was almost over, at that stage on 30-3-66 they received a notice from the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka to the effect that government has acquired suit plot No.76 along with other land for the construction of North South Road there-after the- predecessor of the plaintiffs challenged the said notice in Writ Petition No. 265 of 1966 where DIT also contested and ultimately DIT abandoned the plan of acquisition of the said land; thereafter the predecessor of the plaintiff constructed shops and garage over the B schedule land and then let it out to different tenants; the SA Khatian was wrongly prepared in favour of the defendants thereafter the RS record was correctly prepared in favour of the plaintiffs; further case of the plaintiffs is that though Rajendra Nondi had no son in the name of Dezenda Narayan, yet the defendants created a deed purported to have been executed by Dezendra Narayan in favour of the defendants; the plaintiffs also came to know in recent time that one imposter claiming himself as Dezendra Narayan Nondi, instituted Title Suit No. 25 of 1975 impleading one Aferuddin contractor and Afiluddin contractor as defendants before the Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka and upon practising fraud upon the court obtained an ex parte decree dated 23-8-76 in the said suit; it was also detected by the plaintiffs that the defendant No. 33, Bashir Miah in collusion with defendant Nos. 25-27 instituted Title Suit No. 50 of 1978 before the Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka where he also obtained a decree on 6-4-78 in the said Title Suit No.50 of 1978 on the basis of an alleged amalnama executed by Bama Charan Paul and his brothers in favour of said Bashir Miah and on the basis of the alleged rent receipt in connection therewith and on the basis of those papers created by the defendant No. 33, they are trying to enter into possession of the schedule B land. It is also the case of the plaintiffs that the defendants also approached the Martial Law authority for taking over possession in the suit schedule B land, it is also the case of the plaintiffs that the predecessors of the plaintiffs instituted. Title Suit No. 29 of 1979 before the Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka in respect of the suit land but the same was dismissed for default; but the said order of dismissal took place beyond the knowledge of the plaintiffs under the circumstances as aforesaid the plaintiffs brought the suit for a declaration that the ex parte decree passed in Title Suit No. 25 of 1975 was collusive, fraudulent and not binding upon the plaintiffs. 

 3. The defendant No. 33 Bashir Miah, having entered appearance contested the suit upon filing written statement denying the material allegations made in the plaint contending inter alia and Bama Charan Paul and his three brothers having been in possession of the suit land settled an area of 2.08 acres of land in favour of the defendants upon obtaining salami from them fixing annual rent, by way of a korfa settlement, thereafter upon request from the defendant No. 33, Bama Charan Paul and his three brothers granted amalnama in favour of the defendant No. 33 in respect of an area of 2.08 acres out of the said CS Khatian on 6-9-46 and possession was accordingly handed over there-after the answering defendant carried on possession over the same upon payment of rent to the Zaminders obtaining receipt and he has been in possession of his purchased land upon growing paddy and enjoying usufructs there-from ever since 6-9-46, the date on which the amalnama was executed in his favour by Bama Charan and his three brothers; the defendant. No. 33 also claimed title by adverse possession owing to peaceful possession over the same for more than the statutory period. It is also the case of the defendant No. 33 that the said 2.08 acres of land was wrongly recorded in SA Khatian in favour of late Zamir Bepari son of the Afiluddin, Khaleque Bepari son of Kadom Bepari and the Collector of Dhaka, therefore, the defendant No. 33 brought Title Suit No. 50 of 1978 impleading those persons as defendants for correction of record of rights in respect of said 2.08 acres of land and eventually got a decree in his favour in the suit on 24-3-78; thereafter on the basis of the said decree in Title Suit No. 50 of 1978 the defendant No.33 prayed for correction of record of rights in respect of the SA khatian whereupon Miscellaneous Case No. 50 of 1981 was registered before the ADC (Rev) Dhaka and in that proceedings the ADC having considered the materials on record including the investigation reported submitted before him, passed an order dated 23-9-81 to get the record of right corrected in favour of defendant No. 33, on the basis whereof the record of right i.e. SA khatian was prepared in the name of the defendant No. 33, as such, he has been in possession of the suit land upon payment of rent to the government. It is also the case of the defendant that the plaintiffs have no right, title, interest or possession in the suit land, therefore, the suit is liable to be dismissed.
